drawings.description: à gauche, un croquis : le carré de sommets $1, i, -1, -i$ dans le plan, les points du réseau $\mathbf{Z}[i]$ marqués, un carré plus petit inscrit, centre $o$
drawings.kind: square lattice: square 1, i, -1, -i with lattice points
drawings.notes: Re-read on a tight crop of p. 4. The square with vertices 1, i, -1, -i drawn as a dashed diamond, the horizontal axis between -1 and 1 and the vertical axis through i (solid inside, dashed beyond the diamond); a smaller solid square on the lattice lines, open on its right side as on the page, with the lattice points marked (seven heavy dots) and the centre o; three sides of a pencil frame around it. The labels i, -1, 1 are read on the crop; the -i at the bottom is overinked and placed after the transcription. A second similar sketch lower on the page (a diamond inscribed in a dashed square, at about y 0.66-0.75) is covered by no mark.

drawings.description: à gauche, un croquis : un carré hachuré découpé en quatre, sommets $e$, $\eta'$, $\eta''$, $\eta$
drawings.kind: hatched square cut in four
drawings.notes: A square cut in four by its medians, the quarters hatched, vertex labels e (bottom left), eta' (left), eta'' (below), eta (inside, right of centre, as read); around it faint pencil strokes of a larger tilted square.

drawings.description: à gauche, un croquis : l'hexagone de sommets $\pm 1$, $\pm\zeta$, $\pm\bar{\zeta}$, le réseau et ses points marqués
drawings.kind: hexagon of the Eisenstein lattice with marked points
drawings.notes: Re-read on a tight crop of p. 8. The hexagon with vertices zeta (upper left), -zeta-bar (upper right), 1 (right), -zeta (lower right), zeta-bar (lower left) and the unlabelled vertex -1 (left), its three diagonals through the centre (the half towards zeta heavy with an arrow, the half towards 1 heavy with an arrow); the lattice lines through the six ringed points of the next shell, drawn as a star of David (two triangles), the ringed points, the small lattice points and an open point below the centre; pencil lines from a point above the hexagon down to the centre, to zeta and towards -zeta-bar, and a pencil stroke at the upper left. Labels read on the crop as zeta with a bar or a minus sign (the bars are short strokes above the letters); -1 is not written. Stray pencil strokes to the right belong to another sketch and are left out.

drawings.description: à gauche, un croquis : l'hexagone subdivisé en triangles, un losange de quatre petits triangles repassé en gras. Le « 12 » des arêtes surcharge un autre chiffre. Le reste de la page est blanc ; la suite paginée par lui s'arrête ici, à sa p.~6
drawings.kind: hexagon subdivided into triangles
drawings.notes: Hexagon L, TL, TR, R, BR, BL with its three diagonals through the centre O, and in the upper right the lattice of small triangles (edge 1/2 of the side): the lattice points are computed once as the midpoints of the half-diagonals and of the sides TL-TR and TR-R, and every stroke is drawn between them, so the lattice lines meet exactly there. Heavy strokes (all overdrawn on the page): seven small triangles of the upper right, the half-diagonal O-BR and the right half of the horizontal diagonal; thin: the rest of the outline, the left half of the horizontal diagonal, the half-diagonal O-BL, and the left half of the top side. Dots at the three lattice points he marked (middle of O-TL, O, middle of O-R). The heavy rhombus of four small triangles of the transcription is not singled out from the other heavy strokes. A short pencil stroke at the lower left (no head visible) is drawn; the "12" (in the text, overwriting another figure) and an ink blot under it are left out. Still differs: on the page the hexagon is wider on the left (the lattice is not regular), and the strokes are curved and overshoot; the lattice points are where the drawn lines cross, to within about 1.5 units. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: sous ces deux lignes, deux croquis : un tétraèdre au crayon aux sommets tronqués par de petits cercles ; à droite, un tétraèdre à l'encre dont la subdivision barycentrique est tracée en rouge, avec, en marge :
drawings.kind: two tetrahedra: truncated vertices; barycentric subdivision
drawings.notes: Left (first pass, checked again on the colour render): a pencil tetrahedron, its vertices ringed by small circles (truncation), the hidden edge in short dashes, a stroke across the upper part; the pencil shading is left out. Right, re-read on a colour crop of p. 17: the ink tetrahedron (four vertices, the five visible edges, small arcs ringing three vertices) and, in red, on each of its two visible faces the triangle joining the midpoints of the sides (midpoints as red points, the strokes from the midpoint of the common edge heavy) with a black dot in the middle of each of its sides, each dot joined in red to the opposite vertex of the face.
drawings.disagreement: The red strokes are not the barycentric subdivision proper: on each visible face he draws the medial triangle and joins the midpoint of each of its sides to the face vertex opposite (the medians stop at the medial triangle and never meet at a centroid).

drawings.description: en haut, une suite de croquis de sphères : à gauche une sphère à équateur avec quatre flèches ; au centre une sphère dont l'équateur porte les points $a, b$ et, au-dessus, $c, d$, d'où partent quatre flèches : vers le haut, marquée $\rho$, deux sphères et un tétraèdre ; vers la gauche, marquée $\sigma$, une sphère méridienne et deux sphères accolées, avec la lettre $\ell$ au-dessous ; vers la droite, deux sphères ; vers le bas, deux sphères et un tétraèdre
drawings.kind: sequence of sphere sketches with arrows
drawings.notes: Redrawn on the earlier sphere-by-sphere reading of the colour crops of p. 19, with these changes: labels at \small; the upward arrow from the central sphere, which the earlier file drew twice, drawn once; the upper tetrahedron rebuilt on four vertex points (the inner vertex was two different end points before), all six edges between them, the right one thick; the lower tetrahedron and the arrows from the centre cross of the left sphere already met at single points. Left: a sphere with its equator, four arrows from a centre cross and four points. Centre: the sphere whose equator carries a, b (front) and c, d (back), with four arrows: up (rho) to two spheres with a heavy meridian half and a tetrahedron; left (sigma) to a sphere with a red meridian and heavy equator, l below, then two spheres side by side with red points; right to a sphere with a red meridian and a sphere with nested parallels; down to two spheres with meridian and equator carrying red points and a tetrahedron with two red edges. The red is red-brown pencil on the facsimile (Rd style). Still differs: the dotted (back) and solid (front) halves of equators and meridians are schematised, the number of dots in his dotted strokes is not kept, and each sphere outline is drawn once where he doubled it. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: sous ces mots, un croquis d'un prisme ou d'une pyramide carrée, au crayon et à l'encre ; puis un petit parallélogramme dont un sommet est marqué, et, à côté :
drawings.kind: sketch of a solid (prism or square pyramid); parallelogram with marked vertex
drawings.notes: Under "Carre oriente": a solid with apex A joined to the left vertex (a doubled stroke, drawn once), to a middle right vertex and to the right vertex; the right vertex, the middle right vertex and the bottom vertex on one line (the right outline); the left vertex joined to the middle right vertex (the edge drawn red-brown in the earlier pass, ink on the page) and to the bottom vertex. Five vertex points, every edge drawn between them. Faint pencil: a broken vertical stroke inside (dashed) and a short stroke near the top, both drawn pencil; the long red-brown arc down the right of the sketch (from above the apex) in Rd. Below, the parallelogram: upper left vertex a heavy point, upper right a dot, lower right an open point, lower left a dot, with the curved rotation arrow over the marked vertex. Left out: the dots of the earlier redraw at the vertices of the solid, which are not on the page. Still differs: which solid is meant (prism or square pyramid) is not decided by the drawing; the pencil strokes are approximate; the arc is a stain-like brown stroke whose colour is a reading. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: dessin en marge gauche : un graphe à sommets pondérés $0$, $13$, $4$, $2$, $0$, $3$, $1$, avec arêtes multiples, une boucle en $0$ et des arêtes libres ; au-dessous, sous « 2° », un sommet $0$ avec deux arêtes libres, et un sommet $3$ portant une boucle
drawings.kind: stable graphs (MD graphs: weighted vertices, multiple edges, loops, free edges)
drawings.notes: Encoded from tight crops of p. 46 (three stable-graph/1 encodings) and rendered from the data, with the vertex positions, edge curves and free-edge ends read off the page. First graph: seven vertices weighted 0, 13, 4, 2, 0, 3, 1 (as the transcription lists them): a triple edge between the left 0 and 2 (two arcs and a straight stroke), a loop at the left 0 (one side faint), a double edge 13 - 4, single edges 13 - 2, 4 - 2, 4 - 0, 2 - 0 (right), 2 - 1, 0 (right) - 3; free edges: two at the left 0 (one faint), three at 4, one at the right 0. Derived: b1 = 6, so by his genus formula of p. 48 (g = sum of the weights + rank H^1) the type is (g, nu) = (29, 6); every vertex is stable (2g - 2 + n > 0). Below, under "2°" (the transcription's reading; the earlier "2 deg" reading is dropped): a vertex 0 with three free edges (one short, one long and faint, one curved), type (0, 3); and a vertex 3 with a loop, type (4, 0). The faint strokes are drawn like the others: they leave the vertices like the inked ones and nothing marks them as struck. The first pass missed the third A-B edge and the vertex 3 (at the end of the edge from the right 0).

figures.what: under "2°": vertex 0 with free edges; vertex 3 with a loop

drawings.disagreement: Under "2°" the vertex 0 carries three free edges on the facsimile (one faint), where the transcription says two.

drawings.description: dessin en marge gauche : des sommets isolés pondérés $g_0$, $g_1$, $g_2$, $g_3$, $g_4$, portant chacun quelques arêtes libres, réunis par une accolade. La parenthèse sous $A$ se lit $\vec{A} \setminus \vec{A}^{\sigma}$ sans certitude
drawings.kind: stable graph with isolated vertices (MD graph with only free edges)
drawings.notes: Encoded as one stable-graph/1 with five isolated vertices of symbolic genus g_0..g_4 and no edges, and rendered from the data with the positions read off p. 48: g_0 with three free edges, g_1 and g_2 bare points, g_3 with four free edges, g_4 with one; a brace on the right gathers them. Derived: five components, b1 = 0, nu = 8 free edges; the genus of each component is its weight (his formula g = sum g_s + rank H^1 with H^1 = 0). Stability is not claimed on the page and depends on the genera (g_1, g_2 bare: stable only for genus >= 2; g_4 with one leg: genus >= 1); the checker's valence test reports it false. The label read g_2 by the transcription looks like "g" followed by a tilde-like stroke on the facsimile; the reading g_2 is kept.

drawings.description: Dessins de la page. À gauche, à l'encre rouge et noire, la sphère à trois trous $0$, $1$, $\infty$ subdivisée : sur le bord du trou $0$ les points $a^0_1, \ldots, a^0_4$ et $b^0_1, \ldots, b^0_5$, sur le trou $1$ les points $a^1_1, a^1_2, a^1_3$ et $b^1_1, \ldots, b^1_4$, sur le cercle extérieur $\infty$ les points $a^\infty_1, a^\infty_2, a^\infty_3$ et $b^\infty_1, \ldots, b^\infty_5$, reliés deux à deux par des arcs. En dessous, des cercles orientés, dont l'un marqué « $[0, \alpha][1, \beta)$ » (lecture douteuse), et deux triangles de sommets $0$, $1$, $\infty$ : le premier avec $\alpha = 3$ (points $a_1, a_2, a_3$ sur le côté $1\infty$), $\beta = 5$ ($b_1, \ldots, b_5$ sur $0\infty$), $\gamma = 4$ ($c_1, \ldots, c_4$ sur $01$) ; le second avec la suite « $c_1 c_2 c_3 c_4 \cdot b_5 b_4 b_3 b_2 b_1$ ». Au centre, un petit triangle subdivisé ($b_1, \ldots, b_5$, $a_1, a_2, a_3$, $c_1, \ldots, c_4$) ; à droite, une carte trivalente et les régions $A_{0\infty}$, $A_{01}$, $A_{10}$, $A_{1\infty}$, $A_{\infty 0}$, $A_{\infty 1}$ au crayon
drawings.kind: page of drawings: subdivided pair of pants, oriented circles, subdivided triangles, trivalent map, sphere with three points
drawings.notes: Whole half-page, redrawn on the earlier crop-by-crop reading of p. 66, at a larger scale (1 unit = 3 mm) so that the labels can be set at \small. Changes: every point a^0_i, b^0_i, a^1_i, b^1_i is put exactly on its hole circle and every pencil arc of the pair of pants starts and ends exactly on those points and on the outer circle (its outer ends now marked by dots, the points b^inf_i, a^inf_i); the ticks c_1..c_4, b_5..b_1 of the large triangle 0, 1, infinity are centred on its sides, and in the small subdivided triangle the ticks b_1..b_5 and c_1..c_4 and the dots a_3, a_2, a_1 lie on its sides; the edges of the trivalent map and the arcs of the pencil sphere end on their points. Content as before: left, the sphere with three holes 0, 1, infinity (circles in red ink, each with an orientation arrow; a small pencil rotation sign and a pencil infinity), the twelve pencil arcs joining b^inf_i - b^0_i, a^0_i - b^1_i, a^1_i - a^inf_i; below left four oriented circles (one with a chord and six marked points, one open arc marked [0, alpha][1, beta), doubtful reading kept, two small ones); centre the triangle with gamma = 4, beta = 5, alpha = 3, the pencil triangle with "c_1c_2c_3c_4 . b_5b_4b_3b_2b_1", the small subdivided triangle; right the small trivalent map (schematised), two long pencil strokes and the region labels A_{0inf}, A_{01}, A_{10}, A_{1inf}, A_{inf0}; lower right the pencil sphere with three ringed points and its bundles of arcs. Left out: all the text and formulas of the page, the small labelled graph inside the text at the top centre, and an "A" overwritten near b_3 of the small triangle. Still differs: the arcs are schematic curves, and the trivalent map is schematised. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.
drawings.disagreement: Region label A_{inf 1} listed by the transcription is not found on the crop (five A-labels seen). The pencil sphere at the lower right is the one the transcription mentions in the \note before the mark.

drawings.description: page de dessin, qui revient au découpage en pantalons des pages 66-69
drawings.kind: triangulated map with nested pants curves; weighted trivalent graph
drawings.notes: Whole half-page; the encoding (04-2.json, cellular/1) is unchanged, and the rendering is redrawn from it at a larger scale (1 unit = 3 mm) so that all labels can be set at \small; every edge of the triangulation and of the trivalent graph ends exactly on its vertex point. Left, encoded: a pencil triangulation with eleven ringed vertices (the rings in red ink) and thirteen triangles; the seven vertices of the outer cycle each carry one half-line going off, joined in the encoding at a point at infinity (12 vertices, 30 edges, 20 triangles, chi = 2). The edge 2 - 7 is stroked twice and encoded once. Around it, in red ink, eight nested closed curves forming a chain, the innermost enclosing the vertices 2 and 7, each next one adding one vertex (8, 4, 1, 6, 9, 10, 3); vertices 5 and 11 and the point at infinity lie outside the outermost. The small ticks where the curves cross the edges are left out. Right, redrawn (method 2): a trivalent graph, a hexagon with pendant edges and a loop, ink numbers 19, 7, 1, 15, 17 and small pencil numbers, ringed (1), (2), (3), placed as on the page; not encoded, since whether the numbers weight the vertices or the edges is not fixed by the picture. Caption "decoupages pantalonesques d'une carte (triangulee)" at the top right. Still differs: the red curves are schematic. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Revised 2026-11-11 after Michel's check (#142): the drawing is right against the transcription.

The transcription reads « Nine and nine, as in the transcription »; the page has Eleven ringed vertices, eight closed red curves (Michel, #142: the drawing is right).

drawings.kind: rhombus inscribed in a dashed square grid, marked points
drawings.notes: The dashed frame: a square cut in four by its two medians, continued by one dashed cell above and one below (three sides each). The rhombus joins the midpoints of the sides of the square; its lower right side is heavy. Marked points: the centre, the midpoints of the four sides of the rhombus (five dots), and one dot at the upper right near the corner of the upper cell; a heavy stroke from the centre halfway to the top vertex, dotted below the centre. Second sketch of the kind on the page (the first is 01-1); no labels. drawings.description: à gauche, deux croquis de la sphère : le premier, biffé ; le second avec l'équateur (l'arrière en pointillé) et quatre points marqués, $\eta'^{q}$ et $\eta^{q}$ à l'arrière, $e^{q}$ et $\eta''^{q}$ à l'avant.
drawings.kind: sphere with equator and four marked points (beside a struck sphere)

The right one is drawn: the outline, the equator (front half solid, back half dashed), two dots on the back half and two on the front half, with the labels eta'^q and eta^q above the back dots, e^q and eta''^q under the front dots. drawings.description: à gauche, première sphère, au crayon et à l'encre : l'équateur et trois méridiens issus du pôle nord ; le fuseau de gauche hachuré en rouge, celui de droite hachuré au crayon ; les pôles en rouge, des points noirs sur l'équateur, et de petits hexagones de points autour de deux sommets de l'équateur et d'un point du méridien central.
drawings.kind: sphere with equator and meridians, one lune hatched in red
drawings.notes: Colour render of p. 17. Pencil outline; north and south poles as red points; three meridians from the north pole down to the equator: the left one in red, the middle one in red (pencil below the equator), the right one red-brown; all three continue in pencil to the south pole. The lune between the left and middle meridians is hatched in red (horizontal strokes), the one between the middle and right meridians lightly in pencil (oblique strokes). Equator: heavy red between the left vertex and the middle point, heavy black from there to the right vertex, thin beyond; its back part dashed on the left with a black dot, another black dot at the back right. Small rings of six dots (hexagons) around the left and right vertices on the equator and, dashed, around a point just right of the middle meridian inside the upper hemisphere. Still differs: the number and slope of the hatching strokes are schematic; the ring of dots in the hemisphere sits by eye; the outline is doubled on the page and drawn once. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: au-dessous, seconde sphère : un équateur et quatre points (un en haut, un en bas, un petit cercle à droite sur l'équateur, un groupe de quatre points à gauche). À sa droite, au milieu de la page, un petit croquis d'une sphère à quatre trous (« pantalon » à quatre jambes), la ceinture marquée en rouge.
drawings.kind: sphere with equator and four points; small sphere with four holes
drawings.notes: Left: a sphere outline in ink; a dot at the top and one at the bottom of the outline; the front of the equator from the left edge to a small open circle on the right; on the left of the equator a cluster of four dots; the back of the equator dashed on the left only. Right (figure 2): a small surface with four tubular ends, each closed by a small ellipse, and two red strokes across its waist. Left out: a small squiggle with dots on the back of the first sphere, above the equator (unread; a hole or a point seen from behind). Still differs: the four-holed surface is schematic. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: au milieu, à droite des sphères, un tétraèdre à l'encre verte et brune : deux arêtes opposées repassées en noir, l'arête cachée en pointillé vert ; un trait noir épais joint les milieux de deux arêtes opposées et deux traits verts épais le relient au sommet du haut et au sommet du bas ; du sommet du bas part une flèche vers la note de la marge droite.
drawings.kind: tetrahedron with a heavy H-shaped graph, arrow to the margin note
drawings.notes: Colour render. Four vertices; the edges top-left, top-bottom and right-bottom thin, in brown; the edges top-right and left-bottom heavy black over green; the hidden edge left-right dotted green (with brown dashes on the page). A heavy black stroke joins the midpoint of the top-left edge to the midpoint of the right-bottom edge (both midpoints computed); a heavy green stroke from the top vertex and one from the bottom vertex end on it. Two black dots below the heavy stroke. An ink arrow passes under the bottom vertex and points to the oblique note of the right margin (« ça fait 2^4 - 1 = 15 positions … »). This is the figure the note of the transcription calls « un grand tétraèdre tronqué, arêtes vertes et brunes, pointillés verts »: it is not truncated (the truncated one is the next figure, lower on the page). Still differs: the brown dashes doubling the dotted edge and the exact places of the two dots. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: plus bas, un grand tétraèdre aux quatre sommets tronqués (de petites ellipses brunes), arêtes vertes et brunes, l'arête cachée en tirets bruns ; à l'intérieur, en vert, deux graphes en forme de H joignant les quatre trous, l'un en trait plein épais, l'autre en pointillé.
drawings.kind: truncated tetrahedron with two H-shaped graphs (pants decompositions)
drawings.notes: Colour render. The four vertices are cut off by small brown ellipses (holes). Edges: top-left and top-bottom-right and right-bottom-right in brown; top-right and left-bottom-right in green, heavy; the hidden edge left-right in brown dashes. Inside, in heavy green: a broken line from the middle of the left face to the right edge, joined by a vertical stroke to the top hole and by a short stroke to the bottom-right hole (an H: the holes top and bottom-right on one side). In dotted green: a second broken line from the same left point to the right edge, joined by dotted strokes to the left hole and to the right hole. The pencil tips of the uncut tetrahedron beyond the four ellipses are left out. Not named in the notes of the transcription, whose « grand tétraèdre tronqué » mixes this figure with the one above (01-12). Still differs: the strokes of the two graphs are placed by eye; where the dotted strokes end on the ellipses is approximate. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.kind: sphere with equator, four points and two meridian circles with arrows
drawings.notes: Colour render of p. 18. Faint pencil outline (drawn pencil). Equator in black ink, front half solid, back half dotted, with two dots on the front and two on the back, each placed on the ellipse. Two meridian circles through the poles: the first through the front-left and the back-right points (front half brown above the equator and heavy green below; back half brown dashes above, green dots below), the second through the front-right and the back-left points (front half heavy green above and brown below; back half green dots above, brown dashes below). drawings.kind: tetrahedron with barycentric subdivision of two faces, red dotted square map
drawings.notes: Colour render. Four vertices as dots; the outer edges thin, in brown; the edge common to the two visible faces heavy green. In heavy green, the three medians of each visible face, drawn through the computed centroid of the face and ending at the computed midpoints of the sides.
